Product Photography Pricing: What a Shoot Costs in 2026

Product photography pricing depends on three things: how many images you need, how hard the product is to shoot, and who shoots it. This guide gives you typical rates, the prices studios publish as of November 2026, the line items that push a quote up, what food shoots cost, and how AI compares, so you can set a budget before you ask anyone for a quote.
How much does product photography cost?

What drives the price

How Much Does Product Photography Cost?
There is no single price, but the ranges are well established.

, a photographer booking network, puts average product photography rates at $35 to $170 per image, with the gap explained by setup time, lighting, editing and post-production. Experience moves the price most:
In practice: simple white-background catalog images sit at the low end, styled lifestyle images in the middle, and on-model or campaign images at the top.
How Product Photographers Charge

On top of the photographer's fee, a quote can include models, stylists, hair and makeup, props, studio or location hire, retouching, usage rights, rush delivery and shipping your products to a remote studio. Ask for these as separate lines so you can compare quotes fairly.
Prices Studios Publish (as of November 2026)
A few studios list their prices publicly. These are the figures on their own pricing pages as of November 2026; check the pages before you book, because prices change.
$39 per photo, $93 per video clip. Non-members pay a $149 studio pass per booking; memberships start at $13 a month billed annually.
From $0.95 per image on the $95 a month Professional plan
Squareshot, a remote studio that also published its prices, has closed and no longer takes bookings.
What Drives Product Photography Prices
Reflective, transparent, tiny or very large products need special lighting, more setup time or focus stacking. Jewelry, glassware and electronics with screens cost more than boxed goods.
Number of products and images.
White-background catalog shots are the cheapest; styled lifestyle scenes cost more; on-model shots add talent, styling and approvals.
Models, stylists and props.
Talent is usually billed by the hour plus a usage fee, and props and backdrops are passed on to you.
Some quotes include commercial use; others license images by channel and duration, and charge more for ads, packaging or print.

(Community Accommodation and Support Agency), a not-for-profit disability and child protection organisation, has grown rapidly in recent years. Operating across regional and remote ares of the Northern Territory, New South Wales and Queensland, with recent expansion into Western Australia, their workforce has doubled to around 700 employees in just five years.

“It’s really fast-paced. We’ve got full-time, part-time and casual staff and a high turnover in our frontline support staff, which means we’re always recruiting. At our busiest, we’re hiring 20 to 50 employees a month across multiple locations,”

“We had so much manual handling. Everything was separate. One system for onboarding, one for recruitment, another for compliance. None of them talked to each other. It was really hard to keep up. We were spending all our time chasing documents, some employees requiring filing over 15 documents, cross-checking spreadsheets and making sure people were compliant,”

“Upper management have commented on the performance management processes too. It allows a transparent process and documentation. Managers and employees can access their assigned supervisions and annual appraisal templates and reports, everything they need in one place. It creates a culture of trust and is a lot more productive.”
